$comment: Golden corpus for the [OPTIONS:] / [OPTION-ACTIONS:] marker grammar, consumed by BOTH
the pytest suite (test/test_marker_corpus_parity.py) and the vitest suite
(website/src/test/markerCorpusParity.test.ts).
WHY this file exists. The grammar is hand-mirrored across two languages: constants.py and
optionMarker.ts each re-derive the temper, the sibling lookahead and the tail. Nothing made
them agree. The proof that the pair drifts is already in the tree -- the [OPTIONS:] head is
case-SENSITIVE on the backend and case-INSENSITIVE on the frontend, a divergence this
change had to add per-head casing machinery to work around rather than inherit. Parallel
hand-written tests could not catch that, because each side's suite only ever asked its own
implementation what it thought.
It lives in the protocol module deliberately: that directory is already the cross-language
authority the backend reads from (see TestTheTwoLanguagesAgreeOnTheActionEnum, which
extracts KNOWN_ACTIONS from options.ts rather than restating it).
FIELDS -- every one computable on BOTH sides, so a mismatch is a real disagreement:
text     : the input.
options   : content choices. backend _parse_options / frontend parseOptions().options.
hasAction : would an action chip render. backend _has_option_actions (a bool by design --
it never returns the entry) / frontend parseOptions().action !== null.
stripped  : both heads removed and trimmed. backend strips with OPTIONS_RE_LINE and
OPTION_ACTIONS_RE_LINE (the shape at slack/handler.py) / frontend
parseOptions().text.
A case where the two implementations genuinely disagree carries `divergent` instead of the
three shared fields: `divergent.backend` and `divergent.frontend` each hold the same trio.
Both suites assert the two halves actually DIFFER, so a resolved divergence fails too and
forces the case back to a shared expectation rather than leaving a stale claim of drift.
Do NOT add a case whose expectation you have not measured on both sides.

cases.name: action marker only -- the zero-turn row
CASING DIVERGENCE -- the action head is case-insensitive on BOTH sides
CASING DIVERGENCE -- a lowercase OPTIONS head: the two sides DISAGREE
$comment: MEASURED, not assumed: this corpus disagreed on its first run and this is what it
found. The backend does not treat a lowercase content head as a marker
(OPTIONS_RE_LINE carries only re.MULTILINE, and constants.py documents excluding
OPTIONS: from _CASE_INSENSITIVE_MARKER_HEADS on purpose). The frontend does treat
it as one, because OPTION_MARKER_RE carries the `i` flag.
Recorded per-side rather than reconciled: making either side match the other
changes shipped [OPTIONS:] semantics for every existing caller, which is a
compatibility decision and not one a conformance test should make as a side
effect. Pinned on BOTH sides so neither can move unnoticed, and the parity suites
assert the two values genuinely differ -- so if the divergence is ever resolved,
this case fails and must be collapsed back to a shared expectation.
